entries.title: Trademark check: 'decision-grade' has a live USPTO filing and heavy third-party use
entries.detail:
Checked before anything using the term is published. USPTO serial
87896620: a live (suspended, not dead) 2018 application for the
standard-character mark DECISION-GRADE in Class 042 - analytics
services, AnalystOS's own category. Beroe Inc. separately uses
'Decision Grade Intelligence' as core branding in procurement
analytics, an adjacent category. Stronger risk than a plain web search
for 'no trademark found' would suggest.

Recorded as an owner decision in ROADMAP.md; nothing changed in the
drafts, since nothing using the term is served anywhere. Get real
trademark advice before publishing drafts/defined-analystos.json or
using the term anywhere public.

1212 tests, OK (docs only, no code change).

checker that does not exist to run. Every rule (definition length,
expiry-not-derived, https basis, the fourteen forbidden entry keys, the
seven forbidden citation keys) is proven to actually fire against a
constructed violation, not only asserted against the one real fragment.

/defined/<slug> pages that do not exist in site/ yet - exactly the
mistake the 18 Nov document named and said not to repeat.

updating the test, so this cannot be silently closed by accident.

entries.title: Slice 97: a playbook for document-analysis, acceptance as a check
entries.detail:
drafts/playbook-document-analysis.json validated against the real,
published @flashyos/playbook@0.2.0 (richer than the integration docs
suggested: a closed 13-key catalogue of collaboration types with roles,
steps, after-dependencies and four evidence kinds - a hand-authored
document outside that catalogue still validates). coordination accepts
scope, research gathers sources (closing on attestation, never a
published URL), analysis and verification both close against the real,
unauthenticated POST /api/v1/verify, evidence closes on sealed evidence
(honestly unverified today - Track C does not exist - checked for real
with verifyEvidence and no verifier, not merely asserted), client-delivery
closes on a signed-link URL.

analystos/l4/acceptance.py::document_analysis_acceptance is real product
code, built entirely on the already-tested verify_bundle, requires the
source text (its absence is a failure, not a free pass), never raises.
Its CRITERIA constant is the same text the playbook's seal-the-report
step brief uses, so the two can't silently disagree.

tests/test_playbook.py proves both against this repo's real running
Flask app and seal verifier, including a negative case (self-attestation
refused) showing the real validator's checks are not vacuous.

entries.title: Slice 96: measures/1, computed from the real audit log
entries.detail:
analystos/api_v1/measures.py answers each live role's measure from fields
analystos/api_v1/store.py already writes on every analysis (tier, proposed,
dropped, seal_ok) - no new instrumentation. tier == 'written' is only
reached after both quality gates pass (analysis role's own measure);
dropped/proposed is the verification role's; seal_ok is the result of
actually re-running verify_bundle at delivery time, the evidence role's.

tests/test_measures.py writes real events through FileStore.append_audit
and checks the numbers against the real chained log. Empty denominator is
null, never a fake percentage; the measure sentence is always copied from
the charter; the window is always stated, never derived from the clock.
tools/build_measures.py --check replays the same window/store rather than
diffing against a moving 'now'.

In drafts/, not site/.well-known/: Flashy committed to pull a measures
document on 21 Nov but never confirmed a path or format. Unlike the
charter draft, nothing here could assert anything false if served today
(every value is honestly null, since Slice 84 left production's audit log
dormant) - it is a draft because the path isn't agreed, not because the
content needs guarding.

entries.title: Slice 95: draft and validate the seven-role team charter, kept out of site/
entries.detail:
drafts/flashyos-charter.team.json (coordination, research, analysis,
verification, synthesis, evidence, client-delivery), validated for real
against the published @flashyos/aao@0.4.2 and @flashyos/conformance@0.2.3:
zero errors, all five static checks pass, auditProperty level 2 with zero
issues once every role and discovery slug is declared.

Kept outside site/ deliberately: a file under site/.well-known/ is served
on the next deploy whether or not anything links to it, so an ordinary
merge could not accidentally publish a charter nobody decided to publish.
tests/test_seven_role_charter.py::DraftLocationTest holds that boundary.

Not switched live. Declaring four new roles with no agent behind them and
four discovery slugs with no endpoint behind them would be the gamed
metric docs/mesh-identity.md exists to refuse; switching is recorded as an
owner decision in ROADMAP.md, with what it would actually need in
drafts/README.md (six more live agents, a re-minted join-grant token, four
endpoints that do not exist yet).

entries.title: Slice 94: derive the handshake's capabilities from the charter's role names
entries.detail:
The Flashy estate's 21 Nov 2026 reply resolved an open question from Slice 59:
auditProperty grades a handshake with no capabilities at level 1, and a role
name (restates the charter, claims nothing callable) is a different claim from
a discovery slug (claims an endpoint). tools/build_flashyos_handshake.py now
derives flashyos.json's capabilities from the charter, wired into refresh.py.

Checked against the real, published @flashyos/aao@0.4.2 and
@flashyos/conformance@0.2.3 (tools/flashyos-check/, gitignored node_modules,
set up like the Python venv), not a local guess at their rules:
validateCharterDocument returns zero errors, auditProperty returns
{ok: true, issues: [], level: 2}, and removing capabilities is shown to drop
the real validator back to level 1 - reproducing Flashy's own finding rather
than taking it on their word.

ROADMAP.md's Blocked list and session log brought up to date against the
real GitHub history (PRs 86/87/89 merged since the log's last entry; the
seal key is published; the unscaled-table-number rule is the one remaining
owner decision from the overnight run's proposals).

1150 tests, OK. Nothing deployed; nothing sent to Flashy; no live FlashyOS
API called.

entries.title: Fail clean on Anthropic API errors; reconcile ROADMAP.md through Slice 26
entries.detail:
analystos/l2/analyze.py: analyze_document now catches
anthropic.APIError (the common base for every SDK-raised failure - a
hit spend limit, a bad/revoked key, a rate limit, an outage) around
the one API call and re-raises as a clean ValueError, never echoing
the raw exception. Without this, any of those failures would have
passed through api/analyze.py's ValueError-only except block
uncaught, surfacing as a raw, unhandled 500 instead of the same clean
{"error": "..."} shape every other pipeline failure already gets.
Prompted directly by setting up a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and a
monthly spend cap - hitting that cap needed to fail the same honest
way as everything else.

Tests added at both layers (analyze_document directly, and through
the Flask route) using a real anthropic.APIConnectionError raised
from a mocked client - still no real API call, no cost.

ROADMAP.md: reconciled through Slice 26 - it previously stopped at
Slice 24. Adds Slice 25 (universal upload) and Slice 26 (narrated
analysis) under a new "Beyond the original MVP" heading, since both
went past what the tracked phase originally scoped.
